system_description.narrative_title: Converging shocks: rates, energy, tech and geopolitics reshaping the order
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system in the midst of multi-domain stress: energy and regional wars (Middle East, Yemen, Ukraine) are disrupting supply chains and markets even as central banks tighten to fight inflation, driving historic moves in sovereign bond markets. Simultaneously an intensifying tech-security competition (AI, semiconductors, rare earths) and reciprocal economic coercion (asset seizures, sanctions, trade curbs) are re‑wiring alliances and industrial policy, producing feedback loops between markets, politics and military postures. Expect persistent volatility as these processes co-evolve and backreact on each other rather than settle quickly.
system_description.scope: Interstate relations, multinational firms, financial markets (bonds, equity, commodities), energy and shipping routes, global supply chains (chips, autos, fuel), central banks, defence postures, and multilateral institutions — and the interactions among them.
system_description.super_system: The planetary political-economic system: the integrated international order of states, markets, transnational corporations and global commons (energy, information, sea lanes).
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial system (sovereign debt, credit, central banking)
Global energy and commodity system (oil, gas, LNG, shipping routes)
Global technology-industrial complex (AI, semiconductors, rare earths, supply chains)
Regional security complexes (Middle East, Europe-Ukraine, Indo-Pacific)

variables.name: Middle East maritime energy shock
variables.description: Iran, Iran-aligned proxies, Saudi Arabia and Western navies are escalating attacks, blockades and pipeline strikes around the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf export infrastructure, forcing rapid re-routing of oil and LNG flows and jolting global energy markets.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine protracted war
variables.description: Russia's sustained missile, drone and ground campaigns and Kyiv's continued reliance on Western military and financial support are reshaping battlefield dynamics, defense cooperation and European security calculations.

variables.name: US–China trade and industrial rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are intensifying tariffs, investment controls, supply‑chain industrial policies and contestation over critical materials and autos as both seek to decouple and re‑order global manufacturing networks.

variables.name: Global monetary repricing
variables.description: Major central banks' synchronized tightening — led by the Fed and mirrored by other issuers — is driving up yields, re‑pricing risk across bond and equity markets and reallocating international capital flows.

variables.name: AI safety, governance and militarization race
variables.description: Governments and large tech firms are racing to deploy advanced AI while confronting repeated safety incidents, intellectual‑property and regulatory clashes and accelerating military applications, forcing urgent global debates over governance and controls.
